name: AdaPlanner: Adaptive Planning from Feedback with Language Models
authors: Haotian Sun, Yuchen Zhuang et al. (Georgia Institute of Technology)
reflection_type: verbal-self-critique (LLM-as-planner-and-refiner) with environment-feedback-driven plan revision; closely related to search-guided/replanning but no explicit tree search
feedback_source: external environment feedback (text observations from ALFWorld/MiniWoB++); subgoal-level assertion checks detect discrepancies between predicted and actual observations, which trigger refinement. No human labels or ground-truth oracle.
iteration_structure: iterative-refine within a single episode (closed-loop): the agent refines its self-generated plan in-flight via in-plan and out-of-plan refinement, resuming from an intermediate step rather than resetting the episode
reflection_object: action trajectory and plan (the reusable code-style plan program). In-plan refinement integrates parsed observation info into the existing plan/context for better action grounding; out-of-plan refinement revises the entire plan when feedback deviates from predictions. Successful plans are also stored as reusable skills.
requires_training: none (operates solely via prompting; no dedicated training phase)
reward_or_critic_model: self-as-judge / self-as-refiner: the same LLM acts as planner and refiner; environment observations plus assertion statements supply the verification signal. No separately trained reward or critic model.
distillation_target: reusable-skill/workflow: a skill discovery mechanism archives successful plans (code-style solutions) in a long-term skill memory and reuses them as few-shot exemplars for similar future tasks
emergent_vs_engineered: prompt/scaffold-engineered: the closed-loop refinement, code-style prompting, ask_LLM() parsing action, and skill discovery are hand-designed scaffolds around a frozen LLM (text-davinci-002 / gpt-3.5-turbo), not RL-emergent behavior
memory_type: skill-library (long-term skill memory of successful code-style plans) plus a within-episode scratchpad/context for in-plan information
memory_persistence: cross-task (skills discovered on solved tasks are reused as few-shot exemplars for new, similar tasks); information from in-plan refinement persists within-episode
memory_curation_mechanism: retention of successful solutions only (success-gated, append-on-success); retrieved as few-shot exemplars when a new task resembles a stored skill (retrieval-gated reuse). AutoManual later notes AdaPlanner stores only successful paths, not failures.
error_localization_granularity: step-level / block-level: each subgoal in the code-style plan ends with an assertion statement that tests its fulfillment; a failed assertion localizes the discrepancy and triggers in-plan (one-step) or out-of-plan (whole-plan) refinement at that point
intra_task_vs_inter_task: both: intra-task closed-loop refinement (mid-trajectory plan correction within one episode) plus inter-task transfer via skill discovery (reusing successful plans across tasks)
failure_recovery_vs_avoidance: mid-trajectory-recovery: AdaPlanner proactively refines the plan in-flight when observations deviate from predictions and resumes from an intermediate point within the same episode, rather than only retrying in a reset episode
task_domains: decision-making / embodied-text (household tasks) and web-navigation / tool-use (computer GUI tasks)
benchmarks: ALFWorld (134 tasks across 6 types) and MiniWoB++ (9 feedback tasks + 53 RCI tasks)
headline_result: Outperforms SOTA baselines by 3.73% on ALFWorld and 4.11% on MiniWoB++ while using 2x and 600x fewer samples respectively; overall success 91.79% on ALFWorld (GPT-3/text-davinci-002) and 91.11% on MiniWoB++ feedback tasks (93.22% on no-feedback tasks)
baselines: BUTLER (training-based); ReAct and Inner Monologue and RCI (implicit closed-loop with fixed plan); Reflexion; ProgPrompt/Code-as-Policies (code prompting); DEPS (explicit plan refinement with plan selector); CC-Net (MiniWoB++ RL, 23,000+ samples/task)
gains_vs_baseline: On ALFWorld (134 tasks), AdaPlanner (GPT-3) reaches 91.79% vs Reflexion (GPT-3+3.5) 88.06% and ReAct (GPT-3) 61.94% (i.e. +3.73 over strongest LLM baseline). On MiniWoB++ feedback tasks 91.11% vs strongest comparable baseline (+4.11), with 600x fewer samples; on no-feedback tasks 93.22%, comparable to CC-Net which needs >23,000 samples/task.
compute_cost_profile: No training cost (prompting only). Substantially more sample/demonstration-efficient than baselines: 2x fewer samples on ALFWorld and 600x fewer on MiniWoB++; skill acquisition uses at most one expert demonstration (e.g. one 'put' demo on ALFWorld; zero-shot on MiniWoB++). Inference cost is higher than single-pass due to multiple LLM calls for planning, ask_LLM() parsing, and out-of-plan replanning, but the agent refines only on detected discrepancies rather than every step.
known_limitations: Still requires few-shot expert demonstrations to solve complex tasks (cannot yet do fully demonstration-free complex tasks). Depends on the LLM reliably producing the specific function-form code format; later work (AutoManual) reports AdaPlanner underperforms its paper numbers with creative LLMs because the rigid code format is hard to satisfy. Stores only successful trajectories, not failures, limiting learning from mistakes. Code-style prompting is essential (ablation: removing it drops ALFWorld 81% to 46% and MiniWoB++ 93% to 66%).
oracle_or_external_feedback_dependency: env-reward / external-environment-feedback: refinement is driven by environment observations and subgoal assertion checks (binary success/fail signals from the environment), not by ground-truth labels of the answer. It is closed-loop on environment feedback, so self-correction is grounded in external verification rather than purely intrinsic self-critique.
self_correction_efficacy: net-positive in the tested feedback-rich sequential-decision settings: closed-loop in-plan/out-of-plan refinement and skill discovery each improve success rate (shown via ablations), and AdaPlanner beats fixed-plan / implicit closed-loop baselines under the same LLM. Efficacy relies on availability of environment feedback (assertion signals); gains are largest on tasks that provide feedback.
calibration_effect: not-measured (the paper does not study confidence calibration or a reasoning tax; it measures task success rate)
failure_attribution_capability: attributes-failing-step: assertion statements at subgoal boundaries localize which subgoal failed (discrepancy between predicted and observed state), enabling targeted in-plan or out-of-plan correction. It does not provide a formal failure-mode taxonomy.
failure_mode_addressed: Targets brittleness of open-loop/static plans and fixed-plan closed-loop methods that adjust only the immediate action and assume the initial plan is correct; addresses LLM hallucination via code-style prompting; mitigates error propagation in long-horizon, sparse-reward tasks. Relates to MAST-style modes such as failing to recover from off-track trajectories and step-level execution errors.
dataset_or_benchmark_released: No new benchmark released; evaluates on existing ALFWorld and MiniWoB++. Code released at https://github.com/haotiansun14/AdaPlanner.
builds_on: ReAct (Yao et al. 2022); Reflexion (Shinn et al. 2023); RCI (Kim et al. 2023); Inner Monologue (Huang et al. 2022); code-as-plan methods ProgPrompt and Code-as-Policies; DEPS; chain-of-thought / least-to-most planning; HuggingGPT and Chameleon (open-loop planning)
extended_by_or_inspired: AutoManual (2024, online rule/manual building, ALFWorld/MiniWoB++); REPL-Plan / Interactive and Expressive Code-Augmented Planning (2024); ADAPT: As-Needed Decomposition and Planning (NAACL Findings 2024); CoPiC: Code Driven Planning with Domain-Adaptive Critic (2025, directly compares to AdaPlanner); SALA (Self-Adaptive Language Agent 2024); Hindsight Planner (2024); broadly cited in code-based and closed-loop LLM-agent planning literature
on_policy_distillation_link: Not an on-policy distillation method (no weight updates). The closest analog is its in-context skill distillation: successful code-style plans are distilled into a reusable skill library used as few-shot exemplars, conceptually parallel to skill/experience reuse rather than gradient-based on-policy distillation.
sample_efficiency: High: outperforms baselines using 2x fewer samples on ALFWorld and 600x fewer on MiniWoB++; skill acquisition uses at most one expert demonstration per environment (zero-shot on MiniWoB++), versus baselines like CC-Net needing >23,000 samples per task
